highlights: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens; Artificial Analysis scores Fable 5.2 at 65 on its Intelligence Index.
Meituan released LongCat-2.5, a 1.6 trillion-parameter multimodal MoE model, under the MIT License, and ByteDance Seed introduced Seedream 5.5 with 100-round editing and native RGBA output.
Two papers temper popular ideas: weight-space programming gains are inconsistent, and evolved agent harnesses lose tasks they used to solve while gaining new ones.

items.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are the same underlying model: Fable ships with cybersecurity and biology safeguards and is available to all users, while Mythos access goes through the Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs. Outputs are up to 30% faster than the 5.1 models, pricing is $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, and Fable 5.2 reaches 49.1% on FrontierCode 2.0 at Xhigh effort versus 45.5% for Opus 5.5. Claude Code v2.1.321 makes claude-fable-5-2 the default Fable model with 1M context, and Artificial Analysis scores it 65 (#1 / 74) but also reports $26.54 and 46.4 minutes per Intelligence Index task, so budget carefully for anything beyond hard, long-running work.

evidence.quote: Claude Fable and Claude Mythos are the same underlying model. Fable has strong cybersecurity and biology safeguards to guard against misuse, which allows us to make it available to all users.
Organizations pursuing beneficial applications in cybersecurity or biomedical research can apply for access to Mythos through our recently expanded Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs.
They generate outputs up to 30% faster than Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, and they’re available at a lower price: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens.
Agentic coding FrontierCode 2.0 49.1% Xhigh effort 32.4% Xhigh effort 45.5% 42.8% 41.1% Medium effort
At Xhigh effort, Fable 5.2 reaches 49.1%, the highest score of any released model we’ve tested.
Intelligence Updated # 1 / 74 65 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
Claude Fable 5.2 (Max, Default Fallback) scores 65 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it well above average among comparable models (median: 40).
On average, it costs $26.54 per task to evaluate Claude Fable 5.2 (Max, Default Fallback) on the Intelligence Index. At 46.4 minutes per Intelligence Index task

items.title: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5 multimodal MoE weights under MIT License
items.summary: LongCat-2.5 is a native multimodal MoE model for long-horizon agentic tasks, with 1.6 trillion total parameters and approximately 48 billion activated per token, building on LongCat-2.0 to combine visual understanding with agentic coding. The model card lists 88.4 on Terminal Bench v2.1 (70.8 for LongCat-2.0) and 91.9 on BrowseComp. The MIT License keeps usage terms simple, though self-hosting a model this size is a heavy lift.

evidence.quote: LongCat-2.5 is a native multimodal MoE model for long-horizon agentic tasks, with 1.6 trillion total parameters and approximately 48 billion activated per token . Building on LongCat-2.0, it combines visual understanding with agentic coding
Code Agent Terminal Bench v2.1 88.4 70.8
General Agent BrowseComp 91.9 79.9
The model weights are released under the MIT License .

items.title: ByteDance Seed introduces image model Seedream 5.5
items.summary: Seedream 5.5 preserves unedited regions at the pixel level during multi-turn editing, demonstrated across 100 rounds of edits on one image, and can directly generate images with an alpha channel, including full and partial transparency. In evaluations covering Chinese and English text, its severe text corruption rate fell to 0.4% and its minor rate to 1.7%. Transparent-background output means generated elements can drop into design workflows without a separate background-removal step.

evidence.quote: Preserve unedited regions at the pixel level and eliminate color shifts in those areas, while reducing detail loss and image degradation across successive edits. This supports continued work on the same image across 100 rounds of editing.

Directly generate images with an alpha channel, including full and partial transparency. The model carefully renders edges and transparent regions, allowing generated elements to enter downstream design workflows as standalone assets
Seedream 5.5's severe text corruption rate fell to 0.4%, while its minor text corruption rate fell to 1.7%.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 designs three electronic devices whose prototypes worked unmodified
items.summary: Anthropic asked Claude Fable 5.2 to design a speakerphone, a voice-assistant hub, and a handheld virtual pet from short prompts, and Diode Computers built working prototypes from its files without fixes to the circuitry; on Diode's PCB Gym it scored 69% versus 25% for Fable 5. Anthropic notes the devices are still prototypes with no electrical validation, thermal testing, or certification, so treat this as a signal of hardware-design agent capability rather than a production workflow.

evidence.quote: directed human engineers to build prototypes that worked without any fixes to their circuitry.
Fable 5.2 scored 69% on the benchmark, compared with 25% for Fable 5 (Figure 2).
All three of these devices are still prototypes: they haven’t been through electrical validation, antenna tuning, thermal testing, or certification, and they weren’t designed for mass production.

items.title: NetEase Youdao releases streaming ASR model Confucius4-R2T2
items.summary: Confucius4-R2T2 adapts Qwen3-ASR-1.7B on 1,500 hours of Chinese and English audio so that transcript text, once emitted, is never revised, with decoding chunks configurable from 80 ms to 2 s. Code is under Apache License 2.0 and weights under the NetEase Model Use License Agreement. Voice agents and simultaneous translation pipelines that act on each token can avoid wasted work from retracted output.

evidence.quote: It supports configurable decoding chunks from 80 ms to 2 s. The model operates in a monotonic output mode, committing transcript text permanently without revising previous words.
R2T2, short for Real Real-Time Transcription, adapts Qwen3-ASR-1.7B with Longest Stable Prefix (LSP) learning on 1,500 hours of Chinese and English audio.

Code in the accompanying GitHub repository is released under the Apache License 2.0 and is free to use, modify, and redistribute (including commercially) under the terms of that license. Model weights are released under the NetEase Model Use License Agreement

items.title: Opper edits Qwen3.5-4B weights directly into Pac-Man decision model Jevlar
items.summary: Jevlar changes 0.69% of Qwen3.5-4B's weights, each edit computed from recorded activations rather than learned by gradient descent, and scores 3604 over a 100-game run on Opper's JevMan benchmark: above every model entry, below only the hand-written greedy rule at 4450, for about $50 of GPU time. The edits, the notebook of every pass and the 100 recordings are published, making it a complete worked example of weight-space programming.

evidence.quote: Weight-space programming means changing what a model does by writing its weights directly, each change computed from recorded activations rather than learned by gradient descent.
Jevlar's 100-game run on an H100 scores 3604 ± 314, above every model entry on the board and below only the greedy rule it learned from.
Greedy rule the hand-written search, also the teacher 4450 Jevlar, 4B Qwen3.5-4B with 0.69% of its weights edited, no training
Games ran in Modal containers on A10Gs and H100s, about $50 of GPU time in all.
The edits, the notebook of every pass and the 100 recordings are published with the entry.

items.title: PCBRouteAgent pairs an LLM planner with KiCad's router for PCB routing
items.summary: A Global Routing Planner uses board images plus electrical and geometric information to set topology, routing order, and corridors, a Detailed Routing Executor carries this out through KiCad's native routing engine, and unresolved failures feed back as structured revisions. On 247 boards it reaches clean-pass rates of 100%, 94.9%, 100%, and 40% on D2, D3-A, D3-B, and D3-C. The split between LLM planning and a conventional routing tool is a useful pattern for anyone building EDA agents.

evidence.quote: Achieves up to 100% clean-pass rate on evaluated benchmark splits. 📈 Improves performance by up to 36 percentage points over the strongest evaluated baselines on real-world subsets.

items.title: Study finds weight-space programming gains are localized and inconsistent
items.summary: Across 16 editing trajectories on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-9B, modifying only 1,023 parameters yields a 29.45-point gain on MATH-500, but cross-task transfer is uneven and several trajectories end up keeping the original weights because improvements cannot be reliably validated. It is a sober counterpoint for anyone tempted by results like Jevlar.

evidence.quote: We systematically investigate WSP through 16 editing trajectories across seven benchmarks and two model scales ( Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-9B ).
Notably, modifying only 1,023 parameters yields a 29.45-point improvement.
six of the 16 trajectories retain the original weights when candidate improvements cannot be reliably validated.

items.title: Evolved agent harnesses gain new tasks but lose ones they used to solve
items.summary: Evaluating four methods that evolve agent harnesses without weight updates, the authors find that all sixteen evolved agents gain previously uncovered tasks while losing previously covered ones, most reliability gains raise deployment cost, and the highest-scoring agent never yields the largest mean improvement; they propose EvoAudit in response. A single headline score can mislead when optimizing agents automatically.

evidence.quote: All sixteen evolved agents gain previously uncovered tasks while losing previously covered ones.
EvoAudit turns these diagnostics into revisions of select , analyze , mutate , and gate , achieving the best performance.

items.title: StepFun's P^2-MOPD uses expert weights as priors to speed multi-teacher distillation
items.summary: P^2-MOPD treats a linear combination of student and expert parameters as one differentiable model and jointly trains the mixing coefficients and student weights under the on-policy distillation objective. Across four domains at 1.7B and 4B scales it surpasses MOPD's final average recovery in half the training steps, with the 1.7B model reaching 94.7% versus 80.9%. Useful for teams merging several domain experts into one small model.

evidence.quote: Across four domains at 1.7B and 4B scales, P^2-MOPD achieves faster and more balanced recovery than MOPD from the same initialization, surpassing its final average recovery in half the training steps. At the end of training, our 1.7B model reaches 94.7% average recovery, versus 80.9% for MOPD .
#3 Paper of the day · StepFun

items.title: Ollama v0.40.16 adds Ripple Preview, a 65B coding model
items.summary: The release adds Ricursive Intelligence's 65B dense agentic-coding model Ripple Preview (ollama run ripple-preview), cuts Qwen3.8 Flash Next memory use on Apple silicon by about 27 GiB, and stops /v1/responses from silently truncating by default. Worth upgrading if you run large MoE models on a Mac.

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.322 adds fast mode on Vertex
items.summary: Claude Code v2.1.322 adds fast mode on Vertex in the global, us and eu regions, falling back to standard speed if Vertex refuses it.

items.title: OpenAI describes Control Room for tracking and stopping model workloads
items.summary: OpenAI's Control Room tracks model workloads across its research infrastructure and can rapidly stop them when safety or security concerns arise.

items.title: DeepX claims inference up to 100B parameters at less than 5 W
items.summary: According to EE Times, DeepX claims inference for models of up to 100B parameters at less than 5 W.

items.title: Simon Willison: hide agent-written PR descriptions in a details/summary
items.summary: Simon Willison finds agent-written PR descriptions accurate but too long to read, and now writes a short human-approved introduction with the rest hidden in an HTML <details>/<summary> element.
